scope.title: GPU FFT decomposition across on-chip and global-memory regimes
scope.finite_question: For single-precision, batched single-device 1-D and 2-D FFTs over power-of-two or smooth composite sizes, compare (1) a fused workgroup-local Cooley–Tukey/radix implementation when the transform fits on chip, (2) multi-pass Stockham autosort, and (3) a factorized six-step or transpose-based decomposition for larger transforms. How do radix/factor choice, batch count, data order, global read/write passes, transpose cost, twiddle handling, scratch space and local resource limits set the crossover? Include cases where a simpler multi-pass/library-planned path wins. Keep correctness conventions (ordering, scaling and real/complex layout) distinct from performance.
scope.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use exact-version official cuFFT, rocFFT and/or oneMKL documentation or public maintainer source, plus original GPU FFT papers or technical reports. Compare at least three dataflows in one table. Separate algorithmic traffic counts from published timing results; record each source hardware, transform shape, batch, precision, plan/setup accounting and measurement boundary. Include at least one reported win for a locally fused or transpose-based strategy and a counterexample or boundary where fusion, higher radix, or extra transposes lose because of occupancy, insufficient parallelism, resource pressure, or unfavorable layout. Discuss numerical/order contracts only as they affect comparison. Do not infer Intel Arc/Xe2 performance or implementability from another device.
scope.novelty_guard: This is a general GPU FFT decomposition/dataflow collection. It is distinct from R845 event timing (which only mentions an FFT timing case), R854 sparse-triangular dependency scheduling, and R855 direct/im2col/Winograd convolution dataflow. Exclude FFT-based convolution, multi-GPU/MPI scaling, prime-length algorithms, matrix/tensor-core acceleration, local-memory bank-index mapping, generic profiler methodology, model-specific adoption, and any Strata hardware claim.
scope.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 substantive words; at most 7 primary URLs; one comparison/crossover table; source links, exact versions/hardware, applicability and evidence limits. A bounded future experiment design may be described but must not be run.
prerequisites: Public web access to official FFT library documentation and original GPU FFT implementation papers or technical reports.

Official public cuFFT, rocFFT and Intel oneMKL DFT documentation is available; original GPU FFT papers are also available. This comparison needs no local profile, GPU, runtime, process, liveness, build or benchmark result.
